objection.quote: Empirically the sequence is always eventually periodic in the strong sense a_{n+T}=a_n+L. The core idea is that only finitely many primes are "necessary" for the covering condition; later primes appear but don't restrict the admissible residue classes mod L further.
objection.witness: MISSING: a proof that membership of m in the term set is invariant under m -> m + L for every m >= a_1 (not merely eventually), and that counting terms in one window of length L yields T with a_{n+T} = a_n + L for all n >= 1. The quoted passage asserts periodicity as an empirical observation and states the mechanism as an unproved 'core idea'; the file itself says '## Full proof (Not yet complete.)'.
objection.load_bearing: The required conclusion is precisely global periodicity from n = 1; the text offers only an empirical claim of eventual periodicity, so nothing is established.
